ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (arts. 2, 4, 13, 14, 16), as amended by Ley 2/2016; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010, as amended; Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD) as transposed; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (art. 9); mandatory filing of the Declaración de Titularidad Real with the Registro Mercantil and consolidation in the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales administered by the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (Ministry of Justice).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and commercial register extract of each intermediate corporate UBO entity in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial/company registry in the country of origin of the corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961; where the origin state is not a Contracting State, consular legalization through the Consular Office of Spain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copies of valid passports and/or national identity cards of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent certifying authority in the country of residence of the individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial attestation; if executed abroad, Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the state of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official sworn translation (traducción jurada) into Spanish of all non-Spanish statutory documents required for the notarial deed of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator (traductor jurado) appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certification by the sworn translator; no apostille required for translations to Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted by each non-resident founder/shareholder to execute the incorporation deed and file the SL registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence of the grantor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; private non-apostilled powers of attorney are not accepted for Spanish public deed execution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council consolidated lists (1267/1989 and 1718 regimes), and the Spanish Ministry of the Interior terrorist designation list under Ley 10/2010 arts. 14-16 and EU Regulations (EC) 2580/2001 and (EU) 881/2002; Politically Exposed Person determinations (national, EU and international PEPs) are documented under art. 14.3 of Ley 10/2010; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for the offshore marine charter sector classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced; obliged entities and competent authorities have statutory access to the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales for verification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Central Mercantil (RCM) - denominación social certificate service, operated by the Colegio de Registradores de España (www.registradores.org / sede electronica del Registro Mercantil Central); CIRCE portal may be used for integrated online incorporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be written in the Latin/Roman alphabet; Spanish (Castilian) or the co-official languages of Spain (Catalan, Galician, Basque) are standard; a foreign-language name is permissible if written in Latin characters and does not violate Spanish naming rules; the exact denomination certified by the RCM is registered verbatim, with no additional transliteration permitted at registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España (requires prior authorization of the Consejo de Ministros)
Banco / Bank (requires prior authorization of the Banco de España in financial contexts)
Aseguradora / Insurance (requires prior sectoral regulatory authorization)
Real (royal designation implying patronage of the Spanish Crown)
Oficial / Nacional / Central (when implying official state character)
Identical or phonetically and conceptually confusingly similar denominations already registered in the RCM or in another Spanish or EU registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed denomination, the applicant may file an immediate new electronic application with the RCM for an alternative denomination, which is the fastest practical remedy. If a formal certificate application is rejected on substantive grounds, the applicant may file a recurso de alzada before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGRN) of the Spanish Ministry of Justice within one month from notification, pursuant to the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1784/1996, arts. 325-327). If the DGRN dismisses the appeal, the applicant may file a recurso contencioso-administrativo before the Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Audiencia Nacional within two months of the dismissal notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible solely for the registered office (domicilio social) of the SL provided the address is physically located in Spain and mail is reliably received; a virtual mailbox alone is not sufficient for ISIC 5222 offshore marine charter licensing, because the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante (DGMM) requires an established shipping agent and duly appointed vessel operator representative in Spain, together with recognized operational and managerial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% likelihood within the first two full operating years: medium-high risk driven by DGMM shipboard inspections of chartered offshore supply vessels, AEAT substance audits of maritime-sector companies, and Registro Mercantil and notarial verification under enhanced AML/CFT scrutiny.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Central Mercantil (Colegio de Registradores de España)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of the Registro Mercantil Central; approximately EUR 15-30 per name certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fees for the public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) of the SL with standard bylaws and share capital of EUR 3,000
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish notary (territorial district of the registered office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (Real Decreto 1426/1989 scale); prevailing market benchmark EUR 400-600 for a standard SL formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry fee for inscription of the incorporation deed and company file in the territorial Registro Mercantil
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil territorial (Colegio de Registradores de España)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff under the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil; approximately EUR 50-90

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: ITPAJD - operaciones societarias capital duty on subscribed share capital (statutory 1% state baseline; regional reductions may apply)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria / Autonomous Community tax administration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1993 (TRITPAJD), art. 19; statutory 1% of nominal capital of EUR 3,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real) preparation, notarial attestation and filing in the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales via the Registro Mercantil
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary and Registro Mercantil (Colegio de Registradores de España)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial and registry archival tariff; market benchmark EUR 100-200 for UBO form processing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of foreign corporate/UBO documents and powers of attorney (per original document)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille certifying authority in the country of origin of the document
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; USD 30-120 per document depending on the issuing state

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official sworn translation (traducción jurada) of non-Spanish statutory documents, powers of attorney and corporate extracts into Spanish
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 1-58 (SRL formation, capital, by-laws); Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil); Law 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre, de apoyo a los emprendedores, Articles 15-16 (expedited DUE telematic incorporation); Law 14/2014, de 24 de julio, de Navegación Marítima, Articles 145-150 (naviera / ship-fleet operator rules).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name certification); Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office (register of companies); Notaría / Colegio Notarial de España (notarial deed execution); Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for NIF registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation), inscribed in the Registro Mercantil Provincial and processed through the Documento Único Electrónico (DUE) single point of filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada: minimum subscribed capital EUR 3,000, fully paid up at incorporation; capital represented by participaciones (EUR 1.00 nominal each or as by-laws provide); funds must be deposited in a Spanish bank account and evidenced by a bank capital-in-payment certificate (certificado de desembolso) delivered to the notary; non-cash contributions require an independent valuation report; no separate statutory escrow lock-box is required beyond the bank deposit certificate, but the deposit must remain in the corporate account until registry inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION: The founding shareholder, assembled in extraordinary general meeting, RESOLVED: (1) the subscription of 3,000 participaciones, each of EUR 1.00 nominal, totalling EUR 3,000 fully paid-up capital, is ratified; (2) the registered office is established at the address appearing in the by-laws, within the territorial jurisdiction of the Mercantile Registry of [Province]; (3) [Name] is appointed as Sole Administrator (Administrador Único) with the full powers enumerated in the by-laws, including representation before courts, tax authorities, banks, notaries, and the maritime administration; (4) the Sole Administrator is authorized to execute the DUE filing, obtain the NIF, open bank accounts, and procure all operational licenses; (5) all prior acts of the founders are expressly ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Company Name Certificate (Certificado de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid (electronic application via the RMC portal or through the Sole Notary / sole notary automatic system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed name (up to three alternative names, in order of preference) electronically to the Registro Mercantil Central. The registry verifies there is no identical or confusingly similar pre-existing name and issues a non-transferable certificate of negative name certification. The certificate is valid for three months and must be incorporated into the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Completed standard name application form (solicitud de certificación de denominación)
Valid identification of the founding shareholder (DNI/NIE/passport)
Proposed company name(s) stating the intended corporate object
Government fee receipt for the certification process
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused due to similarity or identity with an existing registered name, promptly submit revised alternatives through the same portal; a new request takes a further 3 working days. If the application is queried due to defective documents, rectify the submission within the registry's 10-working-day procedural window; an appeal against a negative certification is available to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Temporary Bank Account and Deposit the Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Spanish credit institution subject to Banco de España supervision (bank of the founders' election)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the company's proposed name at a Spanish bank. Deposit the minimum share capital of EUR 3,000. Instruct the bank to issue the capital deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) specifying the account holder, the amount deposited, and the account number. Present this certificate to the notary at the deed execution stage. The funds remain blocked until the registry inscription is completed.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation deed and projected by-laws (estatutos)
Passport or NIE of each founding shareholder
Proof of residential and business address
Tax residence certificate of foreign corporate shareholders
AML/KYC forms declaring beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank challenges KYC documentation, provide additional beneficial-ownership declarations and proof of source of funds; if the account is refused, select another supervised bank. If funds are frozen, file a mediation request with Banco de España's customer claims department. The bank certificate must be revalidated if the notarial deed is signed more than two months after issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Colegio Notarial de España (appointment may be facilitated by the Sole Notary/Colegio Notarial automatic designation system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present to the notary the name certificate, the bank capital deposit certificate, the draft by-laws (estatutos), and the founders' details. All founders must appear personally or be represented under a special power of attorney. The notary verifies the legality of the clauses and the required share capital payment, and the parties sign the escritura de constitución. The notary issues a first (primary) copy for filing with the tax authority and registry.
required_dossiers: Certificado de denominación social (valid name certificate)
Bank capital deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso)
Draft by-laws (estatutos) signed by all founders
Passport/NIE copies of all founders
Certificate of corporate existence / legal capacity if a founder is a legal entity
Notarial fee payment (aranceles notariales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues observations (e.g., an illegal by-laws clause), amend the clause and re-execute the deed; minor corrections may be ratified by an acta notarial. If a founder cannot attend, obtain a special power of attorney with express authorization for the incorporation; any refusal by a notary may be remitted to the Colegio Notarial for alternative notary assignment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for the Provisional NIF (Tax Identification Number) with the AEAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), provincial tax office of the company's registered address, or AEAT electronic office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of signing the deed, submit to AEAT the first copy of the deed (primera copia), form 036 (declaración censal de alta), and supporting documents, requesting interim NIF. AEAT assigns a provisional NIF effective for 6 months, which must be converted to a definitive NIF after the commercial registry inscription. The provisional NIF is necessary for all pre-registration communications.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Form 036 (censo de obligados tributarios) duly completed
DNI/NIE of the appointed administrator
Proof of the provisional NIF request authorized by the administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT returns the application for missing information, cure the deficiency within 10 working days of the notice. If the deed copy is defective, obtain a testimonio or second copy from the notary. Disputes concerning the censal registration can be resolved through AEAT's electronic office with a written solicitud followed by a complaint (recurso de reposición) within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Deed with the Provincial Commercial Registry for Inscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (submission through the DUE platform or directly)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the second copy of the notarial deed to the Provincial Commercial Registry together with form 036 stamped by AEAT within two months from the deed date. Pay the applicable state registration duty. Upon review, the registry issues a positive inscription (inscripción), which confers full legal personality on the company. The inscription certificate is used to obtain the definitive NIF from AEAT.
required_dossiers: Second copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
AEAT stamped form 036
Proof of payment of the registration fee (aranceles registrales)
Valid name certificate and bank deposit certificate annexed to the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a calificación negativa (query), respond with corrected documents within the statutory 15-working-day term or, if impossible, request an extension. Where the notary must amend the deed, re-sign and re-submit; an appeal may be filed before the Registro Mercantil Central as a recourse against the registrar's decision. Any delay caused by the registry does not extend the two-month deed filing deadline; therefore file immediately after deed execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure Definitive NIF, Register IAE and Complete Post-Incorporation Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and the provincial labor, tax, and social security offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the registry inscription certificate, return to the AEAT office to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF. File form 036 with the appropriate activity classification, including the IAE economic activity heading for maritime vessel chartering (epígrafe correspondiente to ISIC 5222 / group 8xx where locally applicable). Register the company as an employer with the Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social if it will hire crew or shore staff, and execute any town-hall operating declarations required for the registered office.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry inscription certificate (certificación de inscripción)
Provisional NIF certificate issued by AEAT
Form 036/037 for definitive registration updates
Corporate bank account details and official corporate email
Labor and social security registration forms if hiring personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF is not issued within the stated SLA, submit a written solicitud via the AEAT electronic office and, subsequently, a recurso de reposición; late IAE enrollment penalties may be waived for first-time procedural errors if the company proves good-faith filing. Engage a local asesoría fiscal for immediate correction of censal data.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de la Marina Mercante (General Directorate of the Merchant Marine), Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, in coordination with the Capitanía Marítima of the vessel registration port and the Registro Especial de Buques y Empresas Navieras.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Empresa Naviera / Autorización de Armador y Registro en el Registro Especial de Empresas Navieras, together with flag-state vessel registration (abanderamiento) in the Registro de Buques y Empresas Navieras; each chartered vessel must carry an ISM Code Safety Management Certificate and a Documento de Cumplimiento de Gestión de la Seguridad (company DOC).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO), Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoria B - Comunicación Ambiental / Registro (environmental communication and registration tier); a full EIA report is not required for the leasing of offshore supply vessels by a non-constructing commercial operator, but is triggered only where the company undertakes physical port or offshore infrastructure works (Annex I project thresholds under Law 21/2013 de evaluación ambiental); the operator must file an annual environmental communication with MITECO and maintain waste-management contracts with port reception facilities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: All chartered vessels must comply with MARPOL 73/78 Annex I (oily-water separator and 15 ppm discharge threshold), Annex IV (sewage), Annex V (garbage), and Annex VI (marine fuel sulphur content ≤ 0.50% m/m globally and ≤ 0.10% m/m in emission control areas such as the Mediterranean and North Sea/Baltic, with NOx Tier III limits inside ECAs); EU Regulation 2015/757 (MRV CO2 monitoring, reporting, and verification) applies to ships above 5,000 GT calling at EU ports; Ballast Water Management Convention requires BWMS installation and an approved ballast water management plan; oily waste and cargo residues must be delivered to authorized port reception facilities under Directive 2000/59/EC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: each vessel under charter must hold a valid SOLAS Safety Equipment Certificate, a Safety Construction Certificate (hull, machinery, and electrical surveys), and a radio and navigation safety certificate; structural and load line surveys per the International Load Line Convention are required before flag registration, with periodic class inspections by an IACS-classification society (e.g., Lloyd's, DNV, BV). Onshore: the Spanish registered office must pass municipal fire-safety inspection and occupy a building with a first-occupancy license (licencia de primera ocupación) covering commercial use; workplace health-and-safety clearance is required under Law 31/1995 PRL for administrative employees; additionally, the company must adopt an ISPS Code-compliant security plan if operating in SOLAS-regulated ports, and an occupational medicine service contract must be in force for any crew or shore employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; operative registration forms: modelo 036 (self-registration in the Census de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores), modelo 037 (simplified variant for SMEs), and the notarial/registry procedure for corporate incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign persons forming a Spanish SL: (1) obtain a provisional NIF for the société from AEAT (via modelo 036) at the time the public deed of incorporation is executed before a Spanish Notary Public; (2) record the deed in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central / Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office); (3) after registry inscription, return to AEAT with the registry certificate to receive the definitive Spanish NIF (letter plus 8 digits) with updated modelo 036; (4) non-resident shareholders/directors must separately apply for their NIF-ES (modelo 030 or 036) and appoint a tax representative resident in Spain where AEAT requirements or the regime of the Non-Resident Income Tax so demand; (5) the SL must file an annual annual accounts deposit and interactive Census declaration (modelo 036/037 modifications) whenever capital, activity, or management data change. For the impugnante the SL is also obliged to register in the IVA Census before commencing the leasing activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the SL is a resident corporate taxpayer under Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; Spanish-situs worldwide income is taxed at a 25% headline CIT rate; shareholders are separately taxed in personal/ corporate income tax on distributions, and no partnership flow-through is available for an SL).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box flow-through election exists in Spanish corporate law. Statutory alternatives relevant to the vessel-leasing group: (a) optional tax consolidation (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal, articles 55-70 LIS) available to resident groups holding at least 75% interests and filing consolidated tax returns; (b) special tonnage-tax regime for eligible ocean-going ships (article 113 LIS, applicable to vessels registered in the Spanish or Canary Islands special registry under EU State-aid clearance), which the entity may elect for qualifying offshore support vessels; (c) the cash-basis VAT scheme (régimen de criterio de caja) available below EUR 2,000,000 turnover; (d) mandatory application of EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules (articles 78-81 LIS) that automatically  re-characterize or disallow payments in dual-resident and hybrid instrument/structure mismatches; (e) the option to petition binding advance pricing agreements and tax-rulings through AEAT for maritime-charter margins.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA, Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido; Ley 37/1992 del IVA and RD 1624/1992)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover exemption threshold exists for VAT registration: any taxable person habitually carrying out business or professional activity in Spanish territory must apply for a NIF and register in the IVA Census (modelo 036) before commencing operations. Simplified and special regimes apply only for certain SME categories (e.g., simplified regime below EUR 250,000 annual turnover in eligible sectors), and the cash-based accounting is restricted to businesses below EUR 2,000,000 of annual turnover. Non-established suppliers of B2B services uploaded through the reverse-charge mechanism (for which the Spanish customer is the taxable person) also require a NIF-ES and, where applicable, the registration for an agent/representative. For this offshore vessel charter, the Spanish SL chartering to non-residents generally triggers no positive Spanish output VAT under place-of-supply rules, while charters to Spanish-established customers require full IVA registration without threshold relief.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Large enterprises (annual turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000) and VAT groups must file near-real-time invoicing records with AEAT via the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) system using authenticated SOAP/XML-API calls (services SII-IS, SII-FI, SII-IV y SII-CM), with each invoice submitted within 4 days from issue/entry; all taxpayers must use certified billing software meeting the anti-fraud specifications of Real Decreto 1007/2023 (Verifact-requirements: incorruptible hash, QR code and electronic delivery of invoice files); in Basque territories (Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa, Araba) the TicketBAI digital stamping system further obliges real-time technical clearance before issuing each invoice, while in Navarra the regional equivalent applies; non-resident operators are equally bound when issuing Spanish invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating with credit (0% VAT) is available under article 21 LIVA for exports of goods dispatched to third countries (including vessels and spare parts) where the goods leave EU customs territory within 90 days after delivery (or within the longer documented transport period, max. 180 days when the carrier itinerary justifies extension). Services directly relating to international maritime transport, including the chartering (time, voyage or demise) and auxiliary offshore support-vessel services, qualify as zero-rated where (i) the customer is established outside Spain/EU (article 69 LIVA), or (ii) the Spanish-established customer cannot demonstrate that the effective utilisation and exploitation takes place outside the EU; conversely, where the vessel's operational and trading area lies entirely on the high seas in third-country offshore fields, the 'effective use and enjoyment' rule of article 70.Dos.5º LIVA moves the place of supply outside the EU, thereby excluding the supply from Spanish VAT entirely. The fulfilment of EU export conditions, including customs supervision by the Spanish Customs Office for the DUA and subsequent departure control results (ATLAS), is subject to documentary proof by the exporter before any refund is properly accepted.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo / AES electronic declaration) accepted by Customs with definitive export status ('Estadística', salida efectiva) from Spanish territory
Consultation of the goods release/leaving record via AEAT's ATLAS departure website, evidencing physical exit from EU territory
Bill of Lading (B/L) or sea waybill accompanied by the vessel's delivery/redelivery certificate (signage of the port authority at the port of destination outside the EU)

Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de banco español acreditativo del cobro de la exportación) demonstrating the collection and shown application of the invoice within the legal collection term, together with SWIFT MT103 transfer confirmations
Charter-party contract, freight invoice and the IMO-vessel maritime despacho/expedition dossier (notificación de despacho portuario) documenting the offshore voyage and platform service locations
Commercial invoice, insurance certificate (certificado de seguro marítimo), and, where applicable, the non-VAT certificate of the non-resident charterer's establishment in a third country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT actively audits offshore-vessel charters under export-compliance procedures (verificaciones del domicilio fiscal, customs exit checks and CIVI-VAC international exchange of information). Any unjustified zero-rating or export exemption triggers retroactive VAT assessment for the affected tax periods, together with full late-payment interest (interés de demora). Quantitative sanctions under Ley 58/2003 General Tributaria: minor infractions 50%; serious infractions 50-100%; aggravated serious infractions for means or amount 75-150%; very serious infractions 100-150%. Fraudulent concealment to reduce VAT beyond EUR 120,000 constitutes a criminal tax offence (Código Penal article 305 and 305 bis) punishable with imprisonment of 1 to 6 years per period, accessory penalties of loss of subsidies and binding electoral or banking records, disbarment from certain maritime registries, publication of sanctions, and monetary fines up to six times the defrauded amount. The burden of proving the high-seas place of supply and the effective third-country exploitation lies on the taxpayer; absence or falsification of any element in the documentation bundle (customs DUA, B/L, remittance certificate) causes clawback for the entire open period, which for essential-tax data can be extended to four years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, the national central bank of Spain, acting within the Eurosystem and the Single Supervisory Mechanism; the Ministry of Economy, Commerce and Business retains the residual responsibility for external-transaction statistical declarations and foreign-investment filings
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a full-currency-convertibility jurisdiction within the Eurozone. The euro is freely convertible and the capital account is fully liberalised under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. No prior Central Bank permit is required for current-account or capital-account payments to or from non-residents. Cross-border profit remittance from a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is not exchange-controlled and is generally permitted after lawful corporate distribution; however, the Spanish paying company must operate the applicable non-resident income tax withholding, generally at the statutory rate of 19% where no tax treaty reduction applies, and must retain the certified board resolution, audited financial statements and the shareholder tax-residence certificate for the remitting bank. For balance-of-payments statistics, the bank may be obliged to file a declarative report to Banco de España under the Spanish external-transactions framework; this is a transparency requirement and does not constitute an authorisation or a conversion restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. An offshore supply-vessel lessor can invoice in EUR, USD or any freely accepted currency, and the resulting proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency bank accounts or converted without Banco de España approval. There is no statutory timeline for converting export or service revenue into EUR. The treasury obligation is documentary: export/offshore charter revenue must be supported by approved invoices, the underlying charter party, proof of services or delivery and bank source-of-funds documentation if requested under Spanish Law 10/2010. Where proceeds are routed through Spanish banks, the transaction may be reported for balance-of-payments statistical purposes if the relevant threshold is met; this is a filing, not a convertibility check.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in EUR/USD / Maritime Escrow Account
Capital Escrow Account / Corporate Treasury Operational Account
Corporate Operational Account / Charter-Hire Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-low for the offshore marine charter model. EU/EEA authorised e-money institutions may passport payment services into Spain, but they cannot take deposits, hold principal balances as custodians or provide full maritime escrow services in the manner of a licensed credit institution. UK-based EMI firms do not benefit from EU passporting after Brexit and would require a Spanish payment-agent arrangement or local licensing. Such digital platforms can be accepted only as ancillary clearing providers for FX conversion, petty expense cards or payment aggregation, while the core capital, escrow and charter-hire account should sit in a Spanish first-tier bank to satisfy Law 10/2010 supervisory expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: True remote account opening is practically unavailable for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced offshore marine charter structure. Directors and ultimate beneficial owners must be identified under Spanish money-laundering law. Non-resident directors may appear before a Spanish notary at the point of company formation or execute an apostilled power of attorney before a Spanish consul; thereafter the authorised representative may attend the account-opening interview. Tier-1 banks normally require at least one director, general manager or granted apoderado to complete an in-person or video interview conducted by an AML-trained branch officer. If the UBO holds citizenship or tax residence in a high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction, physical presence or an extra notarised rapport is commonly demanded.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore vessel flag or bareboat re-charter chain leading to high-risk jurisdiction hits or an opaque beneficial-ownership chain including Panama, the Marshall Islands, the Cayman Islands or Malta.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership chain chart from the Spanish S.L. to each natural-person UBO; certified maritime registry certificates for flag and vessel registration; valid ISM Safety Management Certificate and ISPS security compliance certificates; crewing and manning agreements; International Tonnage Certificate; AML/KYC explanation of each intermediary; sanctions screening reports from EU, UK and OFAC lists; and an independent corporate registry verification confirming registered and beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming charter-hire or disbursements from Latin American or African state-related oil and gas entities, with routing via correspondent banks located in higher-risk corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed offshore support-vessel charter party; original or certified invoice ledger; vessel Automatic Identification System (AIS) tracking for the applicable hire period; Brazil, Mexico, Colombia or Ecuador tax-domicile certificates where counterparties reside; board resolutions approving the transaction; trade-compliance declarations certifying no UN/EU/OFAC sanctioned counterparties or cargoes; and verified complete registry documentation for the vessel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing documentation of the initial capital injection or foreign-currency source, causing refusal to open a capital-escrow account or classification of the S.L. as a high-risk PEP-related entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory share-subscription agreement and Spanish notarial deed of incorporation; six-month account statements from the parent or ultimate funding entity; tax-residence certificate for each UBO; register of beneficial owners extract; NIE certificates for signatories; public deed of capital increase where contributions are subsequent; and a signed covenant letter stating that the funds will be credited to the Spanish capital account and disclosed to Banco de España for balance-of-payments statistics if required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions must be routed through a Spanish bank using a clearly demarcated rail. For incoming payments from EU jurisdictions, a SEPA Credit Transfer to the Spanish S.L. IBAN is acceptable; for non-EEA injections, SWIFT MT103 remains the mandatory wire protocol. The remittance instruction should expressly refer to the public deed and purpose such as 'capital contribution to ES_SL' to prevent reclassification as a shareholder loan. The bank will apply Law 10/2010 source-of-funds checks and, where applicable, process the Banco de España balance-of-payments statistical declaration. Capital funds should land in a dedicated capital-escrow or corporate operating account, and the resolutions, notarised deeds, payment instructions and proof of source must be maintained in the treasury onboarding file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound charter-hire, bunker, crew and supply payments are cleared by SEPA Credit Transfer within the EEA and by SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA counterparties. For documentary trade settlement, Spanish banks provide commercial letter-of-credit facilities under SWIFT MT700 and standby letters of credit under SWIFT MT760 for off-hire, mobilisation or performance guarantees. Escrow-maritime disbursements are acceptable where a Spanish notary or a regulated financial institution acts as escrow agent, releasing funds only upon presentation of the charter-party delivery certificate, inspection report or signed pay-off authorisation. Every outbound instruction must carry a matching vendor identity and apposite purpose narrative to maintain the Spanish VAT, corporate-tax and AML audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD forward exchange contracts entered for bona fide treasury hedging of foreign-currency charter-hire and opex exposure.
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps matching the long-term currency profile of vessel-leasing receivables with USD or EUR liabilities.

Non-deliverable forwards on illiquid or restricted currencies, including MXN, COP and BRL, when the offshore charter model generates structurally mismatched currency receipts; such NDFs are permitted in Spain with ISDA documentation and settlement margin in EUR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (Cuentas Anuales: balance sheet, profit and loss, statement of changes in equity, cash flow statement and notes) plus directors' report, approved by the shareholders' general meeting and deposited at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry); notice published in BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General meeting to approve accounts must be held within six months of fiscal year-end (by 30 June for 31 December year-end); deposit must be made within one month of approval (by 30 July for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine EUR 1,200–60,000 under art. 283 RDL 1/2010; 'cierre registral' (registry lock) prevents inscription of any further company documents until the deposit is completed; two consecutive years of non-deposit triggers a BORME admonition and opens administrative dissolution/strike-off procedure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax annual return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) – Modelo 200, including the offshore vessel tonnage-tax election statements where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period (1–25 July for 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge per art. 27 LGT: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% beyond 12 months, plus late-payment interest (3.75% in 2025), minimum EUR 200; penalty of 50%–150% of the omitted quota under art. 191 LGT; denial of the 'al corriente' tax clearance certificate blocking public tenders, subsidies and maritime charter approvals

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT recapitalative return (Resumen Anual del IVA) – Modelo 390
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 January immediately following the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same art. 27 LGT surcharge scale (5%–20%) plus 3.75% late-payment interest; penalty of 50%–150% of the misstated or omitted VAT quota under art. 191 LGT; minimum fixed penalty EUR 200 for returns showing no quota; surcharges and interest accrue until regularized

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual summary of personal income tax withholdings on salaries and directors' fees (Resumen Anual de Retenciones e Ingresos a Cuenta del IRPF) – Modelo 190
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January immediately following the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without quota: fixed penalty EUR 200; with quota: penalty of 50%–150% of withheld amounts under art. 192 LGT; late-payment interest accrues; AEAT withholds the 'al corriente' certificate required for vessel registration and charter contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of ultimate beneficial owners (Declaración Anual de Titularidad Real) confirming shareholding structure and any share transfers of the Sociedad
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Titularidades Reales – Consejo General del Notariado (Administered by the Notarial General Council)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation window 1–31 July for calendar-year entities; for off-calendar-year entities, within 30 days after approval of the annual accounts; share transfers must be communicated within 10 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under RD 95/2024: EUR 150–600 for minor breaches and up to EUR 60,000 for serious breaches; the registry entry is marked as anomalous, invalidating the UBO certificate required by banks, notaries and maritime counterparties for AML/know-your-customer due diligence

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory where the SL meets at least two of the following three criteria for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets exceeding EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover exceeding EUR 5,700,000; average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory regardless of thresholds for public-interest entities, credit/insurance institutions and companies in regulated sectors; shareholders holding at least 5% of the share capital may also force an audit. Offshore supply vessel leasing entities with vessel assets recorded on the balance sheet frequently exceed the asset threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, RD 1514/2007, amended by RD 1/2021) for individual statutory accounts; IFRS-EU for consolidated accounts of listed groups; accounts must be expressed in EUR, signed by the directors and deposited with the Provincial Commercial Registry.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under RD 95/2024 (which regulates the Registro de Titularidades Reales), the SL must file an annual mandatory confirmation each year between 1 July and 31 July for calendar-year entities, or within 30 days after approval of the annual accounts for off-calendar-year entities. All share transfers must be declared within 10 days of the transfer; the confirmation must identify every ultimate beneficial owner and their percentage of shareholding/control, and the registry provides no exemption for single-shareholder SLs.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $650 – $1,620 (typified annual fee for registered office address and domiciliation agent in Spain)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,200 – $10,800 (typical certified audit engagement fee for a mid-size Spanish SL; higher range applicable where vessel-heavy balance sheet increases inventory of fixed assets)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate. Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory conditions and exclusions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Spain applies tax credits and deductions for qualifying research and development, technological innovation, audiovisual productions, foreign tax, and certain investments. Qualifying shipping companies may elect the tonnage tax regime subject to prior authorization, qualifying vessels, qualifying activities, EU State-aid rules, and maritime requirements. Small entities may benefit from reduced rates under the applicable turnover thresholds and transitional rules. The participation exemption may substantially reduce taxation of qualifying dividends and capital gains from shareholdings. Interest limitation, anti-abuse, minimum-tax, substance, and eligibility rules must be tested separately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Spanish Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency Sede Electrónica. Modelo 202 is used for advance Corporate Income Tax payments. Modelo 220 applies only to entities filing under the consolidated tax regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, with quarterly advance payments where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 is generally due within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Modelo 202 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December; electronic filing is normally available until the 20th calendar day, with the applicable banking-day rule for direct debit. The return must be filed even where no tax is payable if a filing obligation exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish Tax Identification Number, registered address, tax period dates, entity type, activity classification, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or lender is not entered as the taxpayer merely because it owns or finances the Spanish SL. The Spanish SL files using its own Spanish Tax Identification Number. Foreign related parties must be correctly identified in related-party and withholding sections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before Corporate Income Tax based on statutory accounts prepared under Spanish accounting rules or an accepted accounting basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-currency amounts must be translated under applicable Spanish accounting and tax rules. Offshore vessel charter revenue, lease income, operating costs, depreciation, impairment, financing costs, and exchange differences must be supported by contracts, invoices, bank records, and vessel-use evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary book-to-tax adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, financing limitations, related-party corrections, exempt income, and tax depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign group companies require arm's-length support, beneficial-owner analysis, withholding-tax review, and evidence of services or rights actually received. Foreign permanent-establishment risk must be separately assessed for vessel operations and personnel.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of eligible prior-period tax losses subject to statutory utilization limits, minimum taxable-income thresholds, ownership-change rules, anti-abuse provisions, and the applicable documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A change in ownership or acquisition of a loss-making company may restrict the use of losses where statutory anti-trafficking conditions are met. Losses must not be used without reconstructing the historical tax computation and supporting the origin and validity of each loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate and gross tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable Corporate Income Tax rate multiplied by the adjusted taxable base, including any qualifying reduced rate or special regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not apply a treaty rate to Spanish Corporate Income Tax. Treaties generally allocate taxing rights between Spain and the foreign state but do not replace the domestic tax computation of the Spanish SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible research, innovation, investment, foreign-tax, audiovisual, employment, and other statutory credits, subject to limits, certification, and carryforward rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes may qualify for relief only within the applicable statutory limits and with official evidence of payment and foreign tax liability. A foreign parent cannot claim Spanish tax credits merely because it funds the Spanish company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax suffered, Modelo 202 payments, and other tax credits available against the final Corporate Income Tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding tax must not be entered as a Spanish withholding unless the Spanish tax rules expressly permit the credit. Reconcile all Modelo 202 payments, dividend or interest withholding, and accounting tax balances to the general ledger and bank evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance after applying advance payments, withholding credits, and permitted deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made through an accepted Spanish payment channel or authorized tax representative where required. Refund claims should include bank-account ownership evidence and complete reconciliation of the tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions with shareholders, group companies, directors, and other related persons, including amounts, transaction type, valuation, and counterparties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report chartering, vessel leasing, management, technical services, crewing, procurement, insurance, financing, guarantees, royalties, and cost allocations with foreign affiliates. Maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing records and consistency between tax, accounting, customs, VAT, and withholding filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Election or application of consolidated taxation, tonnage tax, restructuring, tax-neutral transactions, or other special regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A vessel-related business must not claim tonnage tax merely because it owns, leases, or charters a vessel. Eligibility, qualifying maritime activity, vessel registration, strategic management, flag, EU State-aid, and authorization requirements must be documented before the election.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic submission using an authorized electronic certificate, Cl@ve where available, or an accredited tax representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign directors and shareholders generally require a Spanish electronic certificate arrangement or a Spanish tax representative or authorized agent. The filing receipt, XML or PDF copy, payment reference, and supporting workpapers should be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Potentially relevant returns include Modelo 232 for certain related-party transactions or transactions with tax havens, Modelo 216 for non-resident withholding, Modelo 296 annual withholding summary, VAT returns, and beneficial-ownership or financial-account information where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL must separately review reporting obligations for cross-border payments, related-party transactions, foreign assets, non-resident recipients, and transactions involving non-cooperative jurisdictions. Absence of a payment does not automatically eliminate an information-return obligation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax payable may attract a fixed or percentage penalty under the General Tax Law, generally reduced for voluntary regularization. Where tax is payable, late self-assessment filing generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months, and 15% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest after the 12-month period. Incorrect returns may attract penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on concealment, repetition, fraudulent means, and other aggravating factors. Failure to file Modelo 202 or information returns may generate separate penalties and interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax advance-payment return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency Sede Electrónica.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment periods in April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December, based on the applicable statutory calculation method. Large companies may be required to use the minimum-payment method based on accounting profit and relevant exclusions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish Tax Identification Number, legal name, tax period, financial year end, and applicable filing category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's identification details, not those of the foreign parent or vessel owner, unless the filing is for a different Spanish taxable entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year Corporate Income Tax liability or current-period accounting profit, depending on the statutory payment method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only amounts attributable to the Spanish taxpayer and reconcile current-period profit with chartering, leasing, financing, and related-party entries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory percentage applied to the relevant calculation base, including any minimum-payment rule applicable to large companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent guarantee or group tax policy does not change the Spanish statutory percentage. Special regimes and tax credits must be tested before reducing the payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments already made for the tax period and amount payable for the current installment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile with bank confirmations, tax-ledger accounts, and Modelo 200 to prevent duplicate payment or unsupported credit claims.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may trigger statutory surcharges generally ranging from 5% to 20%, depending on the delay and whether enforcement has commenced, together with late-payment interest where applicable. Incorrect calculation may trigger tax-deficiency penalties and interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions, treaty relief, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation, and anti-abuse rules. Qualifying EU or EEA corporate shareholders may obtain exemption where minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, and anti-abuse conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid tax-residence certificate from the recipient's competent tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test exposure, ownership and holding-period conditions, and any required Spanish declaration or supporting documentation. Apply the reduced treaty rate at source only where the payer has sufficient evidence and domestic administrative requirements are satisfied; otherwise withhold the domestic rate and permit the recipient to claim a refund through the Spanish Tax Agency. File Modelo 216 for relevant non-resident withholdings and Modelo 296 annual summary. Certificates and supporting records should normally be current and retained for the statutory audit period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic non-resident withholding is generally 24% for recipients outside the EU or EEA and 19% for qualifying EU or EEA recipients, subject to the specific statutory category and current rules. Interest and royalty payments to qualifying associated companies in another EU Member State may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive implementation if minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, beneficial-owner, and anti-abuse conditions are met. Tax treaties commonly reduce interest and royalty withholding, frequently to rates between 0% and 10%, but the applicable treaty must be checked by recipient residence and payment type. Technical, management, brokerage, vessel-management, and similar service fees require separate characterization and may be taxable under domestic or treaty permanent-establishment and business-profit rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Generally EUR 250,000 per related counterparty and transaction type, aggregated under the applicable Spanish rules, is the principal threshold relevant to the exemption from full related-party documentation. Local File and Master File requirements are subject to additional exemptions, transaction categories, group-size rules, and content requirements. Country-by-Country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million in the preceding fiscal year. Modelo 232 may be required for specified related-party transaction thresholds and tax-haven transactions.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other internationally accepted methods and valuation techniques where the listed methods cannot reliably determine an arm's-length result
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a single stand-alone Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulation for all companies. Substance is enforced through the General Tax Law anti-abuse rule, conflict-in-the-application provisions, simulation doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, EU anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation, treaty principal-purpose tests, and transfer-pricing requirements. A Spanish SL should maintain real decision-making, appropriately qualified personnel, premises or operational capacity, vessel-management and chartering records, commercial risk control, bank and accounting autonomy, and evidence that services and assets are actually used. A conduit company receiving dividends, interest, royalties, or charter income without commercial substance may lose treaty or domestic exemption benefits and may face reassessment, interest, penalties, and withholding liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax evasion and fraudulent accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating charter revenue, inflating vessel costs, fabricating invoices, concealing related-party payments, using undeclared cash, or claiming fictitious deductions or tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, plus tax, interest, and potential loss of tax benefits. Where the tax defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 in a tax year, the conduct may constitute a criminal tax offence punishable generally by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to six times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and substantially higher fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil liability for unpaid taxes and penalties where statutory derivation requirements are met, criminal liability for intentional participation, and liability for accounting or document offences. Courts may impose professional disqualification and asset measures. Travel restrictions or passport measures may be ordered in criminal proceedings where legally justified; imprisonment is not automatic and requires judicial proceedings and conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length charter rates, management fees, financing margins, guarantees, insurance premiums, or procurement costs to shift profit outside Spain without contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish Tax Agency may make a primary adjustment, impose secondary adjustment consequences, assess withholding or indirect tax, and apply documentation or valuation penalties. Failure to provide required documentation or provision of materially incomplete or inaccurate documentation may generate specific penalties, generally calculated by reference to the affected transaction or tax data, subject to statutory caps.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face administrative derivation liability where they caused or tolerated non-compliance, and criminal exposure where the conduct forms part of intentional tax fraud. Mere use of a low-margin model is not unlawful if supported by functions, assets, risks, comparables, and reliable records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared permanent establishment or false operational location
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating vessels, negotiating contracts, maintaining dependent agents, or conducting core management activities through Spain while claiming that all profits belong to a foreign company with no Spanish taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spain may attribute profits to a Spanish permanent establishment or Spanish resident company, assess Corporate Income Tax, VAT, withholding, payroll taxes, interest, and penalties, and challenge treaty claims under domestic anti-abuse rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for derived tax debts and may face criminal tax exposure where concealment is intentional and the statutory criminal thresholds are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper treaty, EU exemption, or beneficial-ownership claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, royalties, or vessel-related payments through a shell or conduit company that lacks commercial substance, beneficial ownership, or qualifying ownership and holding conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spain may deny treaty or EU relief, assess withholding at the domestic rate, charge interest, and impose withholding and information-return penalties. Anti-abuse rules may also deny participation exemption or interest and royalty exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false residence certificates, sham arrangements, or misleading withholding files may face civil, administrative, and criminal consequences depending on intent and tax loss.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Value Added Tax and customs fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying vessel leases or maritime services, claiming unsupported input VAT, using false export or intra-EU evidence, or omitting taxable Spanish supplies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, repayment of improperly claimed refunds, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties may apply. Serious or fraudulent VAT conduct may trigger criminal tax proceedings where statutory thresholds are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face derived tax liability and criminal exposure for deliberate false invoices, fabricated transport evidence, or coordinated VAT fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained charter deposits, opaque beneficial ownership, sanctioned counterparties, unusual escrow structures, third-party payments, or transactions inconsistent with the vessel's route, customer, or commercial profile without customer due diligence and suspicious-transaction controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, very serious breaches may attract substantial administrative fines, potentially reaching the higher statutory amounts for entities and responsible officers, together with public reprimand, temporary prohibition from holding management positions, or withdrawal of authorization where applicable. Serious and minor breaches carry lower but material fines and compliance measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and officers responsible for the breach may be fined personally and may face management disqualification. Deliberate money laundering may constitute a criminal offence with imprisonment and asset confiscation. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court in criminal proceedings where legally justified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Chartering, supplying, financing, insuring, or servicing a vessel or counterparty subject to EU, UN, Spanish, or applicable foreign sanctions; concealing beneficial ownership; falsifying vessel identity, cargo, route, or end user; or breaching maritime licensing requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, transaction invalidation, asset blocking, license suspension or revocation, seizure, and criminal sanctions may apply under the relevant sanctions, customs, maritime, and criminal laws. Contractual and insurance coverage may also be void or unenforceable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may face personal administrative and criminal liability for knowing or reckless participation. Asset freezing, judicial travel restrictions, disqualification, and imprisonment may be ordered where the applicable offence and procedural requirements are satisfied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or shareholder loans without distributable profits, ignoring net-equity impairment, disguising distributions as service fees, or repatriating funds while insolvent or unable to satisfy tax, employee, lender, or maritime creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Improper distributions may require restitution with interest, director compensation for losses, corporate-law sanctions, insolvency clawback, and tax recharacterization as dividends or hidden distributions. The transaction may also generate withholding tax and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly or personally liable for unlawful distributions, delayed insolvency filings, creditor damage, and tax debts under the applicable statutory conditions. Criminal insolvency liability may apply to fraudulent asset depletion or concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing, document destruction, or obstruction of tax audit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating backdated charter contracts, destroying vessel logs or accounting records, refusing lawful information requests, concealing digital accounting data, or submitting knowingly false tax documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Separate accounting, information, obstruction, and tax penalties may apply. Serious conduct may constitute document falsification, obstruction of justice, or tax fraud, with fines, professional restrictions, imprisonment, and tax reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The individuals who ordered, approved, signed, or knowingly benefited from false records may be prosecuted personally. Corporate limited liability does not protect intentional personal criminal conduct.
